atb_groups.description: Physical assembly table: code -> group per bus, at most 12 leaves per local bus. atbX_grp[g] is the OR of that group's island-gated atbX_sw lines; atbX_en is the OR of all bus lines. Every legal code belongs to exactly one group. Codes and group-vector widths stay fixed; regrouping changes the generated map identity.

atb_policy: ATB0 is the force bus and ATB1 the sense bus. Each bus closes at most one switch (code 0 = all open). ATB1 may select any node. ATB0 may select only device replicas, matching structures and the six overridable bias/reference nodes; selecting an overridable node on ATB0 requires its bias_override bit, and setting a bias_override bit requires ATB0 to select that node, so the internal source and the bench never drive one node together and an overridden mirror is never left floating. Island nodes are disconnected while their island is off; supply monitor taps are not gated so a switched-off island can be confirmed dead. Nodes marked hardware=false have no tap: their codes are rejected on both buses. Core reference-chain nodes (VBG, ROOT_REF, TRK_<island>) carry the force preconditions of analog/core_support/README.md as commit rules instead of override bits. ATB all-off gap: >= 20 ns from deselect to the next select on one bus (atb_switch_dead_time_s; group/pad non-overlap up to 5.7 ns). The break-before-make rule puts a zero commit between two non-zero codes, i.e. at least one 32-clock SPI transaction, which exceeds 20 ns for any SCLK below 1.6 GHz. control_semantics.switch_dead_time_s (4 ns) remains the analog-switch figure for other selects.
break_before_make_rule: A commit may not change one of these fields directly from one non-zero code to a different non-zero code; it must commit the zero (stopped/off/open) code first. Two SPI transactions separate the commits, far exceeding the 4 ns switch dead time in control_semantics.switch_dead_time_s.
cdc_semantics: The register file is clocked only by SPI SCLK and asynchronously reset by RESET_N AND POR. Active fields are quasi-static: they change only on a successful commit, which also toggles commit_toggle. A consuming clock domain that must see a coherent multi-bit value synchronizes commit_toggle through two flops and reloads its local copy on a toggle edge; the next commit cannot occur for at least one more 32-clock SPI transaction. Purely analog consumers see each field change once per commit; stopped-only fields are changed only while their outputs are isolated.
commit_semantics: SPI writes go to shadow registers (write-time range/encoding check per register; fields wider than 16 bits are range-checked at commit). Writing COMMIT (0x06 bit 0) validates the complete shadow (split-field ranges, every rule above, break-before-make against the active set, and - while the legacy payload ENABLE is 1 - that only live fields differ) and copies shadow to active in one SCLK edge, or rejects the commit, keeps the prior active configuration and latches CONFIG_ERROR (control_semantics.illegal). Bit 1 reverts shadow to active.

gating_rule: A control output whose island list is non-empty is driven to all-zero (isolation value) unless every listed island has its switch enabled and reports power-good (or has pgood_override set). Zero is the off/disconnected/disabled encoding of every state, enable, branch and select field. Register contents keep their programmed values; only the outputs are clamped, so re-enabling an island restores the committed configuration. Island status (0x0A): power-good is a ratiometric rail-up flag, so power-good = 1 with debug.island_power = 0 is the back-drive signature (the island rail is being powered through a control, pad or bias path; analog/island_support README I4).

groups.description: Source of each clock domain. internal_pll selects the functional path (clockmux/pll/clocktree as configured); the others connect the named input receiver directly. Allowed for conv_sample and host_clk only.
groups.name: debug.clk_select

Status is read-only at status.pattern.

groups.name: rxmix.offset

groups.description: Master bias generator gf180mcu_ocd_ip__biasgen (README field names bias.*). All resets are the safe state. ref_sel_fine is gated in hardware (fine_eff = ref_sel_fine & ref_sel_coarse) and also rejected at commit. Bring-up order (analog/core_support/README.md 'Register requirements'): (1) islands off, all fields at reset; (2) ena=1 and core.refchain.bgap_ena=1 (sinks 7/3, trim 8), wait >= 100 us; (3) ref_sel_vbg=1, ref_sel_coarse=1; (4) power an island, set core.refchain.dist_en_<island>=1, then the block enables. Per-die trims (bandgap trim, idac2_source) are applied by host software after every reset.
groups.name: core.biasgen

groups.description: Bandgap (README bgap.*) and bias-distribution root trunk-leg enables (README dist.en_<island> = EN_<ISLAND>). Trunk enables are not island-gated: the documented idac2 trim runs dist_en_debug=1 with the debug island unpowered. Bandgap-before-consumers interlock (always-on audit F5, in RTL: rtl/pt_ctl_decode.sv pt_bgap_interlock): the macro holds c_biasgen_ref_sel_vbg and every c_bias_dist_en_* at 0 until bgap_ena has been 1 for 256 SCLK cycles (>= 10 us for SCLK <= 25 MHz; 51 us at the 5 MHz limit: the consumers switch on in the eighth SPI transaction after the commit); bgap_ena = 0 clears it. The fields themselves read back as written.
groups.name: core.refchain

groups.description: Generalized frequency counter instance a (PLL/TX ring; spec/consolidation-pass.md P3-7, rtl owned by the digital hardening agent): counts the selected source against the reference over a window; enable = source != off. Placed at 0xE8 (free tail of the 0x60-0xEF block) because the 0x40-0x5F debug block is full.
groups.name: debug.freq_count_a

groups.description: Generalized frequency counter instance b (CDR ring; spec/consolidation-pass.md P3-7, rtl owned by the digital hardening agent): counts the selected source against the reference over a window; enable = source != off. Placed at 0xEA (free tail of the 0x60-0xEF block) because the 0x40-0x5F debug block is full.
groups.name: debug.freq_count_b

groups.description: Always-on oscillator pt_aosc EN = macro port c_aosc_en (consumers: fc_src[4], the supply/clock monitor time base and debug observation). Live; RESET 0 (always-on audit F2: nothing needs the oscillator before SPI is up and the analog safe-state evidence is at EN = 0). Software can pulse the field 1 -> 0 -> 1 to leave the stuck state F3. While an RF payload runs (ENABLE=1 with payload_iq = 1) the register file forces the output to 0.
groups.name: core.aosc

groups.description: D-CAL-1 per-board calibration record. Direct live fields (no commit needed).

groups.description: Supply / clock monitor rtl/pt_monitor.sv (D-FAULT): fault = any armed requirement that is pending, tripped (sticky cause) or unobservable (monitor clock lost). Time base: the always-on oscillator (core.aosc.enable must be 1), 16.7-25 ns per tick.
